title: Zero-trust identity, RBAC, and keying requirements for Private deployments — requirements clarifications and sign-off checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Capture final product requirements and acceptance criteria for Zero-trust Identity, RBAC, audit logging, and KMS/HSM integration for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. This ticket consolidates open clarifications from engineering and security reviews, records scope changes, and provides a granular sign-off checklist for PM/Engineering/Security/Legal before ship. Background: Customers deploying Redwood Private require deterministic controls for identity federation (SSO/SAML/OIDC), least-privilege RBAC across control and data planes, tenant-scoped audit events (immutable), and customer-managed keying (CMEK with optional HSM). Several engineering spike outcomes have narrowed implementation options (hybrid SAML/OIDC first-class, RBAC on both control plane and runtime agents, KMS integration via KMS adapter). This PRD addendum lists explicit acceptance criteria, fallbacks for scope reductions, and rollout gating conditions.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML/OIDC: Private control plane must support SAML 2.0 IdP metadata configuration and OIDC discovery URL; immediate test flow against customer IdP succeeds with attribute mappings for 'email', 'groups', and 'subject' within a dedicated test tenant.

RBAC: Role schema must support at minimum: org-admin, org-auditor, infra-admin, runtime-operator, developer; RBAC enforcement implemented on control plane APIs and validated by integration tests that exercise token-scoped permissions and deny escalation attempts.

Audit logging: All auth events (login, token creation, key creation, RBAC changes), model deployment events, and admin actions must be emitted to tenant audit streams with immutable event IDs and integrity checks; audit events must include actor, timestamp, request_id, and before/after deltas for config changes.

KMS/CMEK: Customer-managed keys can be configured via KMS adapters (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) with envelope encryption for model artifacts and secrets; test vector demonstrates key rotation without data loss and a documented fallback when HSM not available.
HSM: For customers requiring HSM, provide documented deployment guide and an automated verification script that proves keys are HSM-backed (via attestation fields) in the configured KMS provider.
Telemetry & Observability: Console surfaces per-tenant keying status, last audit export timestamp, and SSO configuration health checks; alerts exist for failed SAML handshakes and KMS API throttling.

E2E Tests & CI: CI must include smoke tests that provision a test tenant, configure IdP (SAML/OIDC), validate RBAC rules, generate audit logs, and perform a CMEK encrypt/decrypt round-trip; results must be green before merge to release branch.

Documentation: Confluence runbook with step-by-step SSO setup, RBAC role definitions, audit log schema, KMS adapter configuration, and troubleshooting must be published and linked in the customer onboarding flow.

Backward Compatibility & Fallbacks: If a customer's IdP doesn't support required attributes, provide a documented manual mapping workflow and a temporary scoped password grant that is logged and time-limited; this fallback must be explicitly approved by Security for each customer case.
Sign-off: PM, Security, Eng-Infra, and Legal must sign off using the checklist below before enabling feature flags for production tenants.
signoff_checklist: PM: Requirements verified against top 5 target customer contracts and documented exceptions recorded.
Security: Threat model updated; SSO threat mitigations and KMS attestation process reviewed.
Engineering: RBAC implemented on control plane and runtime agents; integration tests passing in staging.
SRE/Infra: Audit log retention policy configured, export pipeline validated, and egress requirements documented for customers.
Legal/Compliance: Customer data flow diagrams and contractual language (CMEK/HSM) approved for target regions.
Docs/Support: Runbook and onboarding checklist published; firstline support trained and a playbook created for SSO/KMS incidents.
QA: CI E2E tests green and manual exploratory checklist executed for two representative customer environments.
Product: Rollout plan and opt-in gating approved; metrics and SLOs for auth latency and audit delivery defined.
Customer Pilot: One anchor customer completes pilot with success criteria met (documented acceptance sign-off in Drive).
Release: Feature flags created and verified; release notes drafted and security contact included for immediate post-launch support.
decisions: Adopt hybrid SAML-first approach with OIDC as follow-on; reason: majority of target enterprise customers use SAML IdPs but OIDC enables modern automation.
Enforce RBAC labels in control plane and annotate runtime agents for scoped token exchange; reason: prevents lateral privilege escalation.
Implement KMS adapter pattern with provider plugins rather than direct provider SDKs embedded; reason: easier testing and future HSM vendor swaps.
Audit events will be immutable and append-only with an exportable SHA256-based integrity checksum per batch; reason: legal/audit requirements for tamper evidence.
scope_changes: Removed: Full federated SCIM provisioning from initial launch — scoped to manual group mapping; SCIM to be scoped for Q3 2026.
Added: HSM attestation and automated verification script as a launch-time non-blocking capability for customers requesting HSM (must pass sign-off).
Clarified: RBAC roles and least-privilege default for newly created tenants; previously unspecified developer vs runtime-operator separation now explicit.
rollout_and_testing_plan: Phase 1 (Private staging): Feature flags enabled for internal staging tenants; run E2E smoke tests and runbook walkthroughs.
Phase 2 (Pilot): Enable for 2 pilot customers with assigned Customer Success lead; run daily health checks for 14 days and collect sign-off artifacts.
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout): Ramp to new customers by region with opt-in toggle; monitor auth error rate, audit delivery latency, and KMS error surface for 72 hours per cohort.
Rollback plan: Feature flag off for affected tenants; revoke any temporary credentials; engage on-call security and infra for root-cause and data integrity checks.
Postmortem gate: Any audit loss or key compromise requires a full incident review and a hold on further rollouts until remediation is validated.
notes: 2026-02-25 sync: Security requested explicit attestation fields from KMS providers; Eng to prototype AWS CloudHSM attestation by 2026-03-10.
Tradeoff: Full SCIM would accelerate group mapping but increases surface area and requires additional compliance reviews; deferred to Q3.

Open question: Should credential rotation be forced on key rotation or allow a rolling window? Eng suggests rolling window for availability, Security prefers forced rotation; deferred to implementation spike.
Customer ask: Anchor customer B requested per-model keying — scoped out of MVP but tracked as PM-9001 for roadmap.
Follow-ups: Legal to produce standard CMEK contract addendum; Support to create remediation playbook for SSO misconfigurations.
